Retain the deterministic rootfs-placement failure: vendor/DA/Linux address spaces differed, leaving an old superblock while overwriting the filesystem body. Separate continuous DA verification reads from region-relative writes; never reuse Tempo's partition offsets or automatic installer. # Y2R-600 — M6 recoverable production userspace, updates and security

**Deferred planning epic; no implementation-ready children added by this audit.**

## Goal / why this epic is needed

Connect the diagnostic initramfs to an appliance userspace and eventual safe
Android retirement. Current BOOTIMG recovery is not a production update system.
Track the platform part of later M18–M20; native application tasks stay in its repo.

## Dependencies / evidence

M0 residual backup/lineage knowledge and owner-proven recovery; core storage,
power, logging and native-audio gates. Do not re-prove SPFT viability from scratch.
Use `partition-map.md`, `recovery.md`, `first-experiment-result.md` and M1 runtime
limits. Production distribution choice follows measured footprint/support.

## High-level coverage

Recoverable development rootfs then production image selection (no premature
Debian/Buildroot/Yocto commitment), ARMv7 userspace/toolchain/ABI contract, bounded
boot services and non-root app permissions/udev or narrow privileged service.
Read-only/mutable partition policy, filesystem/power-loss behavior, storage
capacity, service supervision and data migration/backup; no speculative A/B layout.

Complete same-device personalized backup/independent retention and recovery
consistency where needed; preserve stock loaders/calibration and known-good
fallback. Track signed payloads/integrity, interruption-safe install, rollback
and key management/threat model. Update signatures alone do not establish a
hardware verified-boot chain behind unchanged LK. Do not bypass security state.

Pin maintained 6.18.y selection/update process, reproducible release manifests,
firmware/source/license provenance and notices; retain audit traceability.
Define production debug exposure, secret-redacted exports, entropy/identity,
RTC versus network-time policy and certificate needs. Shutdown/recovery, service
restart and update-failure tests precede release qualification and Android removal.

## Exit evidence / unlocks

A measured minimal image boots reliably, supervises the non-root player against
standard Linux interfaces, preserves user/calibration data and can recover/roll
back tested interrupted updates under an approved storage model. Security and
support limitations are explicit. Provides M6 platform contracts for M7+ and the
later M18–M20 release gates; core app development need not wait for full OTA.

## Out-of-scope / stop

No repartitioning, formatting, rootfs install, signing key generation, firmware
redistribution decision or updater implementation today. Stop on uncertain write
ranges/rollback semantics, inadequate backup/power, provenance or privilege gaps.
Do not make a whole-ROM restore the automatic fallback for a BOOTIMG-only trial.

## Execution and validation boundary

High-level planning epic only, not an implementation task or hardware permission.
Expand only the next evidence-backed change when this phase is activated; preserve
existing stable IDs and link existing issues instead of duplicating them. No
speculative driver task list, build, flash or experiment is authorized by this epic.

Before closing the phase or proceeding through its exit gate, repeat the
[standing roadmap/gap audit](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/planning/roadmap-gap-audit.md#standing-milestone-boundary-rule)
using real hardware results. Separate owner reports, retained artifacts, source
support and actual device validation. Unknown dependencies stop the relevant
path; do not guess hardware or silently broaden scope. Milestone qualification
uses the appropriate full verification boundary; small later fixes keep targeted
validation and D08/package checks without routine provenance re-audits.

without treating stock firmware filenames as proof of usable upstream drivers.
FM application work remains the blueprint's later M16 boundary.

## Dependencies / evidence

`docs/knowledge/wifi-bluetooth.md`, `audio-path.md`, stock ramdisk WMT/STP and
firmware inventories; shared power/reset/clock/transport and reserved-memory

Identify exact controller/revision, SDIO/UART/other transport, STP/WMT role,
reset/IRQ/clock/supplies and native driver feasibility. Pin actually selected
firmware, initialization order, calibration/NVRAM/MAC ownership and redistribution
provenance. A vendor 3.4 kernel module is not a v6.18 driver. Preserve credentials,
bonds and unique addresses privately; package no unreviewed firmware blobs.

constraints, WPA capability, reconnect, DHCP/DNS and trusted time. Bluetooth
includes HCI/BlueZ feasibility, pairing/reconnect, A2DP/AVRCP and measured codec

For each supported radio: hardware/firmware/driver provenance plus captured

reception evidence. Gate F unlocks network/BT application services; FM support
unlocks later FM-specific planning. Missing/unpopulated functionality is recorded
explicitly rather than hidden behind a generic connected status.

## Out-of-scope / stop

No network UI, scrobbling, proprietary stack port, bus probing, firmware execution
or calibration writes today. Stop at unproved transport, firmware provenance,

No detailed radio backlog is created before the first bounded identity proof.

Owner reports LK logo followed by black. The exact `out/m2-baseline-03/capture-02/` recording identifies Linux `6.18.0-y2-m2-baseline3`, 480Mbps CDC ACM, and contains **102,314 bytes over180seconds**, SHA-256 `8fb89a7ee79f17a6496aaa24184ebb7596786b33b5e1357cb3ed6145bb966bf6`. All kernel sequences0–605 are present in order; PID1 reaches heartbeat184. Host timeout/exit0 is the end of the recording duration. This directory name does not establish a reconnect test.

Four CPUs remain online with advancing timer/IPIs and IRQ errors0; post-display MemAvailable12,080kB under unchanged D08. Navigation/volume/power produce55 balanced press/release pairs. DRM/fb0/module initialization succeeds, but owner-visible output stays black. Wheel EINT55 fires8times, but eight I2C frame reads time out (-110), controller completion IRQ0. Logging remains responsive through the180second capture. Next combined iteration addresses actual display output and wheel transport, standard state/failure diagnostics, and snapshot framing; no per-register flash sequence or milestone promotion.

Existing 300-second owner limit and M3/M4/M5 exclusions remain.

The owner reports black/grey after LK. BASELINE-02 identifies at 480Mbps ACM and the host sends LOG1, but the 180-second capture retains **zero bytes**, no protocol header, exit2. No kernel/PID1 failure location is established. This is not a successful display modeset or log capture. BASELINE-01 input/SMP/storage results remain historical.

BASELINE-03 carries MediaTek DRM as the sole loadable module in the bounded RAM-only initramfs. After initial provider snapshots and active LOG1 output, PID1 starts a separate finit_module child, stays on CPU0, and reaps with WNOHANG; the child loads on observed CPU1. Kernel/driver logs retain the existing single CDC ACM relay. This isolates synchronous probing from PID1, not global bus/lockup faults. MT6582 DSI host transfers now refuse unpowered MMIO after pre-enable failure. No guessed panel/PLL/rail values or per-register flash.

Capture with the existing tool and `--build M2-INPUT-01`, press/release Prev/Menu/Next/Play/Select and retain the complete logs. No Y2 was attached at host inspection. Hardware acceptance remains open, M1 complete, M2 active/exit blocked; no M3/application work.

---

## Donor implementation scope — 2026-09-09

The owner now authorizes donor-assisted Linux 6.18 core implementation while preserving the canonical tree, stock loaders and BOOTIMG-only manual flashes. The 364-file/36-commit donor bundle at 53fb57bb99c916c24b65db5b7f9723be37f67826 has been inventoried against v6.18 and our hardware evidence. USBACM-03 kernel/PID1 logs remain physically confirmed; USBACM-04 robustness remains pending. M1 complete; M2 active with all exit criteria retained; M3/app and radios deferred.

The rigid #27 → #22 → #23 → #24 → #25 → #26 queue is superseded by actual dependencies. First slice: five GPIO navigation buttons through upstream gpio-keys-polled/evdev and existing USB logs on unchanged D08. An inherited-input GPIO provider refuses output-configured lines and preserves mux/pull/clock/IRQ state. This delivers a standard input path before the EINT/I2C/DMA foundation needed for wheel rotation. Corrected CCF/PWRAP/EINT/I2C, meaningful RAM reconciliation, display/panel/backlight and removable storage/rootfs follow by dependency. No driver or milestone hardware success is inferred from donor source.

Donor risks include approximate PLL/mux rates, a chosen connectivity reservation unlike stock, missing full pinctrl/thermal/DVFS, generic optional-pinctrl errors swallowing deferred probes, unchecked charger/backlight writes and broad display/DMA ownership. Reuse source selectively with licensing/attribution. Existing issues retain their owners; no speculative issue fan-out. One clean input build, full relevant offline suite, ARM input/relay and D08/BOOTIMG validation precede the owner flash boundary.

# Y2H-300 — M2 core platform foundations and boot stability

Canonical epic [#28](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/28); [coverage audit](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/planning/roadmap-gap-audit.md).

**ACTIVE, entry PARTIAL (2026-09-09 owner authorization).** See the
[activation audit](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/planning/roadmap-gap-audit.md#m2-activation-audit--2026-09-09).
USB #27 and the smallest #23 prerequisite come first. Exit remains blocked;
no optional-feature waiver is claimed.

## Current execution checkpoint — 2026-09-09

USBACM-03 logging succeeds on real hardware; source and evidence are pushed in
7ee780a. The verified 45-second capture contains 11,754 bytes, early kernel
sequence 0–77 and PID1 beats 1–43 without sequence gaps or relay errors; exit 0.
[Evidence](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/knowledge/m2-usbacm-hardware-result.md).

The owner now authorizes one bounded #27 late-open/no-reader/disconnect/reconnect
robustness iteration, followed on success by #22 RAM → #23 shared power → #24
evdev → #25 display/backlight → #26 removable SD/stage rootfs → M2 qualification
and closure audit. USBACM-03 terminates at first detach; [USBACM-04 is offline validated and ready for owner testing](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/build/m2-usbacm-04-result.md),
permitting one guarded reconnect within the existing deadline. Hardware
robustness is not yet established. Host metadata identifies Y2 at USB 5-2,
/dev/ttyACM0, 0525:a4a7; direct session capture still needs tty access permission.

M1 complete; M2 active/exit blocked; all coverage gaps and later-phase gates
remain intact. No RAM, DMA, unrelated USB, rail, partition or production scope
is changed by this iteration. No assistant flash or physical-device write.

## Goal / why this epic is needed

Keep the core-hardware exit gate represented beyond the existing five research
issues: a repeatably bootable, observable device with usable memory, display,
input and storage. M1's physical Linux/PID1 success is achieved; exact-hash boot
repeatability, timing accuracy and long-run stability are not yet qualified.

## Existing work and dependencies

Track, do not duplicate: RAM #22, shared power #23, controls #24, display #25,
read-only SD #26, blocked USB logging #27 and optional physical UART #16.
Depend on M1 evidence and the relevant recovery policy, not a new M0 recovery
rehearsal. Share supply/thermal prerequisites with the power epic.

## High-level coverage

- Boot identity/result capture, bounded repeated boots, timer/IRQ accuracy,
  working-set/stress evidence, reset/reboot and kernel regression policy.
- Static RAM expansion/exclusions, optional researched SMP release/coherency,
  complete needed clocks/resets, pinctrl/GPIO/IRQ domains and I2C access.
- Production watchdog ownership, early-to-driver handoff, timeout/reset behavior;
  stopped AP watchdog remains the experiment policy until separately replaced.
- Standard display/panel/backlight and evdev wheel/buttons/power key; determine
  whether stock touch-named nodes imply a physical touch interface on this board.
- USB controller/PHY/device-mode debug; do not hide missing lower-layer drivers
  behind generic compatibles. Preserve the diagnostic path during takeover.
- Removable SD first, later eMMC controller/DMA and filesystem integrity. Define
  a recoverable development rootfs and storage access boundaries with the
  production epic; no automatic reuse of everything after BOOTIMG.

## Exit evidence / unlocks

Reviewable actual-hardware reports demonstrate boot repeatability, adequate
measured memory, observable failures, viable display/input, media access and a
recoverable rootfs plan/implementation appropriate to the phase. No claim that
all 1 GiB, SMP or every peripheral is mandatory for the first wired-player slice.
List any waived optional feature explicitly. Unlocks Gate C device-UI experiments
and the native audio proof, not Android retirement.

## Out-of-scope / stop

Audio playback, radios, complete product PM and application logic are owned by
later epics. Stop a subsystem at missing clock/pin/rail/DMA contracts or loss of
recovery/observation; decompose that single prerequisite when authorized.

## Execution and validation boundary

The owner has activated incremental M2 research and implementation. This epic
alone grants no physical-device permission.
Expand only the next evidence-backed change when this phase is activated; preserve
existing stable IDs and link existing issues instead of duplicating them. No
speculative driver task list, build, flash or experiment is authorized by this epic.

Before closing the phase or proceeding through its exit gate, repeat the
[standing roadmap/gap audit](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/planning/roadmap-gap-audit.md#standing-milestone-boundary-rule)
using real hardware results. Separate owner reports, retained artifacts, source
support and actual device validation. Unknown dependencies stop the relevant
path; do not guess hardware or silently broaden scope. Milestone qualification
uses the appropriate full verification boundary; small later fixes keep targeted
validation and D08/package checks without routine provenance re-audits.

# Y2B-255 — Add bounded USB CDC ACM kernel and PID1 logging

## Current execution checkpoint — 2026-09-09

The owner explicitly requested one combined enumeration/logging candidate to
reduce physical iteration. [Scope audit](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/planning/roadmap-gap-audit.md#combined-usb-ownership-scope-review--baseline-d9c2c98)
keeps M1 complete, M2 active/exit blocked and later phases deferred.
[CHRDET evidence](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/knowledge/m2-chrdet-hardware-result.md) establishes
charger presence under the reported cable conditions; connected-start6a=BE
still refuses wake. No new hardware result has been inferred.

**Immediate next test: [M2-USBACM-01](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/build/m2-usbacm-01-result.md)**,
1,159,168 bytes, SHA-256
`d2d1f8cbbaa23ffcbdeddb317db7a8e62bc21deca9ebebc564c9b55a5590aedd`.
[Reviewed combined contract](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/knowledge/m2-usb-enumeration.md): boot
unplugged, perform the proven guarded wake, attach at the screen prompt, check
fresh supply/clock/PHY/DMA state, apply the FM/LK digital device-session sequence,
then attempt upstream MUSB peripheral PIO, one standard g_serial ACM and bounded
retained/live kernel + PID1 logging. No host VBUS supply, analog calibration,
PMIC writes, active-DMA recovery, RAM expansion or other partition writes.

One clean build passes 23 full-suite methods, one additional linked-syscall
mutation method and 8 observation methods, including 30 QEMU ARM PID1 scenarios
and host/ARM relay faults. Exact DT/config, linked accesses, D08 and BOOTIMG pass.
[Host capture tool](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/build/usb-log-capture.md) is ready. No device operation
was performed. Stop for the owner's BOOTIMG-only physical test within 60s.
USBGUARD-01 remains an optional untested fallback, not a prerequisite test.

This advances offline implementation only. Physical enumeration, real log
continuity, late-open/non-reading behavior and controller reconnect qualification
remain outstanding. The first trial stops on first detach/error or 50s active
window; reconnect and connected-start recovery are not implemented. #23/#27/#28
stay open, and every original hardware acceptance criterion remains intact.
Original drafting-only restrictions below are superseded only for this
specifically authorized/audited experiment, not a general production port.


## Status, type and goal

**Draft implementation contract; BLOCKED on the MT6582 USB controller gate below.**
Not implementation-ready for hardware, and not `state:luna-ready`. The upper-layer
logging design is specified; no implementer is asked to choose PHY registers or
invent a DT compatible. This issue does not absorb an unresearched controller port.

One goal: over the existing Y2 USB data port, retrieve retained kernel messages
and continuing PID1 logs on a Linux PC, independent of screen reading or physical
UART. Exactly one CDC ACM port; no interactive shell.

[Research, source evidence and detailed contract](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/knowledge/usb-logging.md).

## Why now / dependencies

M1 hardware execution and periodic PID1 diagnostics are owner-observed (#20/#21).
Host log access would shorten every later RAM, input, display and storage cycle.
Y2E-160 #23's PMIC/supply research is a prerequisite source for VUSB, not a claim
that USB power is already understood. Physical UART #16, full RAM expansion #22,
input/display/SD implementation are not prerequisites. D08 remains the default.
No reordering/execution of the five queued foundation issues is authorized here.

**Hard gate before any runtime implementation:** record an exact, reviewed
MT6582 USB device-controller contract in `docs/knowledge/usb-logging.md`:

- Controller MMIO span, SPI/polarity, interrupt handling and sufficient FIFO/
  endpoint layout for EP0 + ACM bulk IN/OUT + notification IN.
- Actual clock-provider/gate/48 MHz mapping, USB2 PHY register/initialization/
  calibration contract and VUSB supply/ownership after normal LK handoff.
- Peripheral/VBUS detection and safe disconnect/reconnect; no host VBUS sourcing.
- Quiescence of inherited USB DMA before PIO, without touching display DMA.
- Exact v6.18 glue/PHY compatibility or a reviewed completed prerequisite change.

Stock `musb-hdrc.0` IRQ 64 and public MT6582 SPI32 evidence support the route.
They do not prove that existing `mediatek,mtk-musb` glue plus a sibling PHY works.
Upstream glue needs three clocks and a generic PHY; current Y2 DT provides neither.
Do not unblock until this gate is resolved. If it needs a controller/clock/PHY
implementation, stop and return the single smallest prerequisite for owner review;
do not create further issues or expand this issue automatically.

## Exact implementation scope after the gate

1. Reuse proven MUSB in **peripheral-only PIO mode** with built-in `g_serial`,
   defaults ACM on / OBEX off / one port. Kernel intent:
   `USB_SUPPORT=y`, `USB_GADGET=y`, `USB_MUSB_HDRC=y`, `USB_MUSB_GADGET=y`,
   `MUSB_PIO_ONLY=y`, `USB_G_SERIAL=y`; host `USB=n`, DMA/OTG/dual-role off.
   `USB_MUSB_MEDIATEK` and `NOP_USB_XCEIV` apply only if the exact glue is verified;
   selected GENERIC_PHY/USB_ROLE_SWITCH and the real provider must be accounted
   for. `U_SERIAL_CONSOLE=n`; no `console=ttyGS0` dependency. Existing PRINTK/TTY/
   proc/sysfs/time32 stay enabled. g_serial selects LIBCOMPOSITE/CONFIGFS_FS and
   serial functions; no configfs mount or setup daemon is needed.
2. DT: only the reviewed USB/PHY/clock/supply nodes, `dr_mode="peripheral"`.
   Extend the exact DT validator whitelist, not D08 bounds. No guessed addresses,
   dummy PHY, fake fixed clocks, unrelated clock gating or full-SoC DTS import.
3. Existing native PID1: bounded raw nonblocking `/dev/ttyGS0` relay. Discover
   its dynamic device number from sysfs; read kernel ring through `/dev/kmsg`
   (1:11, read-only). Keep an 8 KiB PID1 startup/status ring, 32 KiB TX queue,
   8 KiB kernel-record buffer. Service at most 16 records / 16 KiB each heartbeat
   pass. Preserve partial writes and report drops/gaps; boot/heartbeat never
   waits for a host. New syscall numbers require actual linked-kernel checks.
4. Host sends only `LOG1\n` to begin/restart replay of retained kernel and PID1
   startup records, then live records/status. Bounded 16-byte parser; no shell,
   arbitrary command execution or writable filesystem/log API. Include kernel
   release, build identifier, source/sequence and explicit overflow markers.
5. Host script selects an explicit verified USB tty path, commonly `/dev/ttyACM0`
   but never inferred from numbering alone. Raw 115200 8N1/no flow control, ACM
   DTR asserted, sends LOG1, records bytes/timestamps/USB identity and exit reason.
   Use upstream standard g_serial descriptors, not stock Android VID/PID. Read
   `/sys/class/tty` USB parent identity; no privileged global host-rule changes.

## Files/components

Prospective edits only: `kernel/config/first-boot.config`,
`kernel/dts/innioasis-y2-first-boot.dts`, `tools/validation/dtb.py`, `initramfs/init.c`
and a small bounded relay helper; `tools/observation/usb-log-capture.py`,
`tests/test_usb_logging.py` and affected PID1/syscall/artifact tests;
`docs/build/usb-log-capture.md`, `docs/knowledge/usb-logging.md`.
Reuse upstream MUSB/gadget code where the gate establishes compatibility. A broad
USB/PHY/clock/PMIC driver port is a prerequisite, not hidden scope here.

## Explicit out-of-scope

Implementation/build/flash during this drafting session; automatic hardware trials;
ADB/adbd, networking, RNDIS/ECM, mass storage, Debian, storage access, app work,
USB host/OTG switching, charging-policy changes, accessory UART muxing, preloader/
LK/security/partition changes, RAM expansion, full display driver, persistent
ramoops reservations and guaranteed pre-enumeration crash/panic capture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hardware prerequisite contract is reviewed and complete; no guessed driver,
  compatible, clock, PHY/power or DMA handoff assumption remains.
- [ ] Resolved config is peripheral/PIO/one-ACM, with expected dependencies and
  real syscall implementations; only approved DT nodes are added.
- [ ] Linux host enumerates the selected Y2 as CDC ACM and opens its tty without
  custom kernel drivers; capture identifies actual USB path/descriptors.
- [ ] One LOG1 capture includes retained early **kernel-ring** messages, PID1
  startup/mount/sleep status and at least ten increasing heartbeat records.
  These are actual kernel logs, not only rendered-screen summaries.
- [ ] Late host open, non-reading host and one authorized disconnect/reconnect
  do not stall PID1; reconnection can replay and reports any overwritten logs.
- [ ] Positive hardware results name candidate SHA-256, host tool/version, raw
  log/hash and timing. Offline fixture success is not enumeration success.
- [ ] D08, CPU0, watchdog and guarded framebuffer fallback remain intact;
  BOOTIMG bounds pass and loader/partition/calibration state is untouched.

Do not close as hardware-success based only on source review or fixture tests.
The issue may remain blocked while upper-layer intent is fully specified.

## Validation

No implementation or device tests in this session. Later targeted host/ARM
fixtures must cover partial/EAGAIN/EINTR/ENODEV/EPIPE writes, ring wrap/overrun,
late LOG1, malformed/overlength input, partial lines, no-reader/reconnect and
continued heartbeat. Check actual linked syscall targets, dynamic tty discovery
and bounded memory/CPU budgets. Replay pre-enumeration kernel records if still
retained; report gaps instead of silently promising lossless delivery.

Initial USB is a **new hardware subsystem**: review controller/PHY/clock/power
and DMA safety, binding/config resolution, affected regressions and complete
D08/layout/BOOTIMG validation under the broader verification boundary. Trust
unchanged pinned source/toolchain/recovery provenance. Subsequent relay-only
changes use one clean build, targeted tests and final D08/package size/hash,
without routine historical full-suite or two-build repetition.

Any later device validation requires a separately authorized BOOTIMG-only trial,
retained known-good fallback and bounded observation window. No flash is
implicitly authorized by implementing or closing an offline checkpoint.

## Stop conditions and alternative

Stop at the controller gate, unexpected PHY/PMIC/clock/reset dependencies,
inherited-DMA uncertainty beyond the approved experiment, IRQ storm, VBUS-source
risk, framebuffer/heartbeat regression, parser bounds failure or D08 overflow.
Do not enlarge RAM or port an entire subsystem to make this issue fit.

No simpler reliable host-readable alternative is established: ADB, USB Ethernet
and vendor bulk all require the same missing UDC/PHY; UART-over-USB requires an
unverified electrical accessory, and ramoops lacks a proven retained range and
reader. Preserve the working screen temporarily; do not call it USB logging.

## Unlocks

Host-retained boot/runtime logs for faster single-change RAM/input/display/storage
bring-up. It does not observe preloader/LK or hangs before USB/PID1 initialization,
and it does not start another platform milestone or Y2PlayerNative work.

**Current status, 2026-09-08: physical UART work remains OPEN/deferred; it is not an absolute launch blocker for the owner-authorized risk-accepted visual experiment.** Y2E-150 #18 implements D13 guarded inherited video; Y2B-240 #19 will collect actual board proof. # Y2E-140 — Establish a reliable first-boot observation path

Depends on Y2E-125/130 and the completed M1 offline artifact. Research directly; supporting host tooling only. No candidate flash, pin probing, voltage injection, boot-mode change or feature expansion.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Reconcile package preloader/LK/kernel UART selection with safe installed-stock console evidence; record exact normal/conditional selection and baud/format.
- [x] Establish a board-specific physical TX/GND connection and logic voltage from credible evidence, or explicitly retain this blocker and evaluate the smallest alternative.
- [x] Define reproducible receive-only host capture with retained raw bytes, timing, adapter/settings and integrity metadata.
- [ ] Capture identifiable stock LK/kernel output before changing BOOTIMG; distinguish a host tooling test from device proof.
- [x] Decide whether the existing artifact needs revision; any justified change must rerun all offline validation.
- [x] Update authoritative knowledge and identify the next bounded launch proof. Keep this issue open if physical/capture acceptance remains unsatisfied.

2026-09-08 result: **OPEN, physical evidence required.** Installed ttyMT0/sysfs/iomem plus remapped FM driver prove the normal installed-kernel controller is UART0 (0x11002000), superseding UART3. Package LK's conditional UART0 branch is consistent with this result, but installed handoff identity/routing and actual baud are not fully proved. The manufacturer native pin-domain table supports expected 1.8 V; no board-specific TX/GND pad or pad measurement is confirmed. No adapter was present.

D10 corrects only DT UART0/IRQ51 and strict validation. Two fresh full offline builds match across 11 outputs; all nine artifact tests pass (22 real-artifact and 25 package mutation/extent cases), source verification covers 91,166 files/links. All D08 addresses/sizes, kernel/config/initramfs bytes stay unchanged. Current BOOTIMG SHA-256: `574061649e10266927267b68afbc95da7fe0761dc9823e88767741bac9363fd9`.

Receive-only host tool/runbook implemented; four PTY tests pass on Python 3.14.7 and locked 3.12.14. These are not hardware proof. Actual ADB `/proc/last_kmsg` yields only a prior late kernel/shutdown log, not LK/serial capture. Next missing evidence is verified UART0 TX/GND/level plus actual stock LK/kernel capture. If native TX is inaccessible, investigate exact preloader UART-over-USB accessory detection/electrical/routing persistence; do not guess cables or switch PHY live. U07b is the next launch gate after observation passes; U07c and backup/recovery/power remain required.

[Authoritative evidence](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/knowledge/observation-path.md), [capture runbook](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/build/stock-console-capture.md), [revised artifact](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/build/first-boot-result.md). No candidate boot/flash or additional Linux feature occurred.

Checkpoints: [7942247](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/commit/7942247) (host capture), [b4fcc12](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/commit/b4fcc12) (evidence and UART0 revalidation). Remains OPEN; no launch authorization.


### Y2E-145 follow-up, 2026-09-08

Owner confirms only ordinary USB/ADB is available. Actual FM preloader tracing identifies the UART-over-USB lead as electrical PHY line-state/accessory detection (0xc0/0x80 at 0x11200620), not an ADB serial service. Its selected UART switch, cable wiring/level and installed handoff continuity remain unproved. No verified physical TX/GND or stock LK/kernel serial capture exists; **Y2E-140 remains OPEN**.

[Full launch assessment](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/knowledge/launch-readiness.md) and [Y2E-145 #17](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/17) record NO-GO, hardware-dependent authentication, missing current BOOTIMG backup and normal-path watchdog risk. Checkpoint: [83f9a24](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/commit/83f9a24). No flash/boot or artifact change.
